title: Dold's Theorem: Cohomological Index for Free G-Spaces
description: Axiomatized formalization of Dold's theorem (1983), which provides a unified cohomological index framework for Borsuk-Ulam type results. The Dold index assigns a numerical invariant to free G-spaces on spheres and shows equivariant maps respect it. From 5 axioms, we derive 11 theorems: classical Borsuk-Ulam (Z/2), Yang-Borsuk (Z/p), composite group bounds, and unification of the buDim framework from OQ02OQ01.

meta.author: Lean Genius (after Dold 1983)
meta.assumptions: doldIndex function (cohomological index), doldIndex_one (trivial group), doldIndex_z2 (Z/2 antipodal = n), doldIndex_prime (Z/p rotation = 2n-1), doldIndex_dvd_mono (Dold's theorem: subgroup monotonicity).
originalContributions: Axiomatized Dold cohomological index with 5 axioms (1 fewer than OQ02OQ01)
Proved borsuk_ulam_from_dold: classical BU as consequence of Dold index
Proved yang_borsuk_from_dold: Yang-Borsuk as consequence of Dold index
Proved z4_index_bound, z6_index_from_z2, z6_index_from_z3: composite bounds
Proved buDim unification: OQ02OQ01 axioms follow from Dold axioms
Complete formalizability assessment with ~1800 line gap analysis

mathlibDependencies.description: Every natural number >= 2 has a prime divisor

sections.title: The Dold Cohomological Index
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the cohomological index doldIndex(g, n) = ind_{Z/g}(S^n) as a function of group order and sphere dimension.
sections.mathContext: The cohomological index is defined via Borel equivariant cohomology: ind_G(X) = sup{k : H^k(BG) -> H^k_G(X) is injective}. We axiomatize rather than construct it.

sections.title: Axiomatized Properties
sections.summary: Four properties: trivial group (index = 0), Z/2 (index = n), Z/p prime (index = 2n-1), and Dold's theorem (subgroup monotonicity).
sections.mathContext: These encode the classical values computed by Borsuk, Yang, and Dold, plus the core transfer-map argument that is Dold's main theorem.

sections.title: Classical Borsuk-Ulam from Dold
sections.summary: Derives the Borsuk-Ulam theorem (no odd map S^n -> S^{n-1}) from the Dold index.
sections.mathContext: If an odd map S^n -> S^{n-1} existed, it would be Z/2-equivariant, contradicting ind_{Z/2}(S^n) = n > n-1 = ind_{Z/2}(S^{n-1}).

sections.title: Yang-Borsuk from Dold
sections.summary: Derives the Yang-Borsuk theorem (Z/p-equivariant obstruction) from the Dold index.
sections.mathContext: For prime p, the Z/p-equivariant Borsuk-Ulam follows from ind_{Z/p}(S^{2n-1}) = 2n-1 strictly exceeding ind_{Z/p}(S^{2n-3}).

sections.title: Composite Group Bounds
sections.summary: Derives index bounds for Z/4, Z/6, Z/pq, and general composite groups from prime subgroup monotonicity.
sections.mathContext: Every composite group inherits index bounds from its prime subgroups via Dold's subgroup monotonicity. These bounds are tight for standard representations.

sections.title: Unification with buDim (OQ02OQ01)
sections.summary: Shows buDim(g, d) = doldIndex(g, d-1) and derives all OQ02OQ01 axioms from Dold axioms.
sections.mathContext: The buDim function from OQ02OQ01 is a repackaging of the Dold index. This unification reduces 6 axioms to 5 while preserving all consequences.

sections.title: Formalizability Assessment
sections.summary: Complete gap analysis: ~1800 lines of equivariant cohomology needed to remove all axioms. Priority: transfer maps (~200 lines) for highest value per effort.
sections.mathContext: The axioms can be proved from singular cohomology + Borel construction + transfer maps. Mathlib currently lacks all three, but they are constructible.
